caption: A tin of formula every five days adds up fast. What did the baby cost that you didn't see coming?

slides.title:
What our baby
really costs us on
R30 600 p/m
Living in Midrand
slides.body:
Him 32, her 30
Married, baby girl (5 months)
Jobs: Logistics coordinator & bank call centre agent
Household net income: R30 600 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: We looked at cheaper. We wanted a second bedroom with a door that shuts.

slides.title: Baby costs
slides.includes: Nappies R1 400, formula R1 650, wipes, clothes, creche deposit saving
slides.body: Formula was the shock. She goes through a tin in five days.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.body: We used to eat out on Fridays. Now Friday is a pot of pap and a baby asleep on someone.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: His car is paid off. Hers is the one we both regret a bit.

slides.title: Medical aid
slides.includes: Hospital plan for the three of us
slides.body: We pay it every month hoping not to use it. The birth used it.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Petrol, electricity, phone, funeral policy, black tax, stokvel, takeaway coffee
slides.body: Takeaway coffee is R450 of that. I won't say whose.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R30 600. We thought we budgeted for a baby. We budgeted for a baby's first month.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded our statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for us.

Formula, nappies and wipes were three separate lines we had always lumped together.

No bank login needed.
